clue.text: Gold best security, ultimately, shown by late investigation

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
'the tops' means the very best

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word security

explanation.surface: A detective's last-minute probe finds gold, the best security, behind it all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' here means dead, as in 'the late king', so the late investigation is one carried out on a body.
explanation.definitionFit: A post-mortem examination is an investigation into how a deceased person died.

clue.text: Shakespearean character, male — figure indicative of opposition

parts.note: Mark Antony appears in Julius Caesar and Antony and Cleopatra

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean hero is cast as the man who opposes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' here means a figure of speech, a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A word of opposite meaning, like hot for cold, signals contrast.

clue.text: You can't foresee what abandoning narrative means

definitions.meaning: an idiom meaning it is impossible to predict
read literally, no telling of a story

explanation.surface: A remark that the future is unknowable, and what giving up storytelling means.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses unpredictability; taken word by word it says no story is told.

clue.text: A name is inscribed in orchestra area identifying instrumentalist

indicators.note: inscribed in means the letters are written inside the orchestra area

parts.note: the orchestra pit sits below the stage in a theatre

explanation.surface: A name carved in the orchestra pit reveals which musician played there.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard player is one kind of person who plays a musical instrument.

clue.text: You once succeeded? Agreed

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a person made it in the past, and the reply is assent.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-word reply of assent stands for 'agreed!' as an exclamation.

clue.text: A lot of food: I tucked in and … indigestion treatment needed

indicators.note: tucked in says the pieces are pushed inside the word and
a lot of, not all of, means the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a taco is a Mexican food

explanation.surface: Someone who has eaten a big meal reaches for something to settle the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed' is a link; the ellipsis is only for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedies for heartburn neutralise stomach acid, which is exactly what this kind of tablet does.

clue.text: Independent involved in chap's radio broadcast — stimulating stuff

indicators.note: involved in means the letter is put among the shuffled letters
broadcast means scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An independent politician appears on a man's radio show to stir things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like part of the radio picture but signals the shuffle; the I goes near the end of the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance said to arouse sexual desire is a stimulant.

clue.text: Appear in court, say, if brought in quarrelsome

indicators.note: brought in means the little word goes inside the other

parts.note: testy means irritable and quarrelsome

explanation.surface: A quarrelsome witness is asked to appear in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving evidence as a witness is the typical example of appearing before a court.

clue.text: Our cat playing with the fibre — a regular game will keep one entertained

definitions.text: regular game will keep one entertained

indicators.note: playing with means toying with the letters, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A cat batting at a strand of fibre is happy with its usual game.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes someone content with a routine pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who sticks to set routines would be kept happy by the same pastime every time.

clue.text: More than one dance step is kept up, maintained by old-fashioned types

indicators.note: maintained by means held inside the word for old-fashioned types

parts.note: a dodo is a person behind the times

indicators.note: kept up in a down clue means the word is is read upwards

explanation.surface: Traditional folk keep up a set of dance steps.
explanation.definitionFit: In square dancing, partners circle back to back; the plural names several such moves.

clue.text: Best stage in development of radio?

definitions.meaning: an old idiom for the very finest thing
the cat's whisker was a thin wire contact used in early crystal radio sets

explanation.surface: A question about the history of wireless technology.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom praises something as superb, and the wire detector was a genuine early wireless component.

clue.text: Wanting information back about Scottish city, in brief

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes round the other piece
back means the word for information is read backwards

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Edin. is the short form of Edinburgh, the Scottish capital

explanation.surface: Someone is short of facts about a Scottish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in brief' signals the standard short form of Edinburgh rather than a whole city name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe lacking something one requires, as in 'wanting attention' or 'needing attention'.

clue.text: A rude dog, not trained, but friendly

indicators.note: trained means schooled into a new shape, the letters reordered

explanation.surface: An untrained dog is rude, but still friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a kind, easy-going temperament is amiable.

clue.text: Failed to provide a hand in the dictionary

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the dictionary's abbreviation

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
a mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry for the word 'hand' was left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving something out means one has failed to supply it.

clue.text: WWI battle — attempt to secure old position — horrific affair

parts.note: Mons in Belgium was the site of a 1914 battle

indicators.note: to secure means the attempt holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to sit is to be positioned somewhere

explanation.surface: A First World War battle where troops tried to hold an old position was a horror.
explanation.definitionFit: Something monstrous or hideous is a dreadful thing, an outrage or atrocity.

clue.text: No time for relaxation? That's the thing about lawyers …

indicators.note: no means the abbreviation for time is taken away

parts.note: rest is relaxation

explanation.surface: Lawyers are so busy they never get time to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: Res is Latin for 'thing', used in legal phrases such as res judicata. The ellipsis runs on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal Latin uses this word to mean a matter or object, the thing in dispute.

clue.text: … and the law — no time at the outset for delicacy

indicators.note: no says the time abbreviation is removed
at the outset places the removal at the start of the word

parts.note: tact is delicacy in dealing with people

explanation.surface: Continuing from the lawyers: the law has no time for tactfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute passed by Parliament is called an Act, so a piece of legislation.

clue.text: Enemy of uprising captured by Robin Hood, say, runs off in the end

indicators.note: captured by means the reversed word is held inside
off in the end means the runs letter is removed from the finish

parts.note: Robin Hood is a famous bowman
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: uprising in a down clue means the little word reads upwards

explanation.surface: An enemy rebel is caught by Robin Hood but runs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Robin Hood, say' is an example of a bowman; 'in the end' says which of its two R letters goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief adversary is a principal opponent.

clue.text: Persuasive correspondence is a sign of success

parts.note: winning ways are charming and persuasive
post is mail, letters

explanation.surface: A convincing letter shows that someone is doing well.
explanation.definitionFit: In horse racing the marker at the finish line shows which runner has won.

clue.text: Meander and chatter in turn? That'll be me!

parts.note: to wind is to meander

indicators.note: in turn means the chatter word is turned back to front

parts.note: gab is chatter

explanation.surface: The clue's voice admits that meandering talk is its own habit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the clue speaking as the answer: a talker who rambles on.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rambles and chatters endlessly is a bore who talks too much.

clue.text: Limited coverage? It's been given some air

definitions.meaning: a skimpy undergarment that covers very little
Bach's Air on the ... names a violin string

explanation.definitionFit: The skimpy garment and the violin string from the Bach title share the name.

clue.text: Racecourse regular's attempt to attract attention during row

indicators.note: during means one piece goes in the middle of the other

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
pst is a sound made to catch someone's attention

explanation.surface: A racegoer tries to catch someone's eye in a row of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gives betting advice on horses is a familiar figure at race meetings.

clue.text: Two ways of restraining former telecommunications operator

parts.note: the phrase 'two ways of restraining' names two holders; the first is a prison cell
the second way of restraining someone is to catch them in a net

explanation.surface: A list of two methods of holding someone back.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'Two ways of restraining' supplies both pieces: a cell and a net.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellnet was a British mobile phone network, later rebranded O2.

clue.text: Draw equal with guy beginning to hesitate in tournament

parts.note: cat is slang for a guy, a man

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the word for a tournament

parts.note: a cup is a knockout tournament

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of hesitate

explanation.surface: A competitor hesitates in a tournament but levels the score.
explanation.definitionFit: To close the gap on a leader is to get back level with them.

clue.text: One not taking serious interest in line penned by storyteller? Recalled it beside the gallows

indicators.note: penned by means the line letter is enclosed by the storyteller

parts.note: a storyteller in the sense of a liar is a fibber

indicators.note: recalled means the word it is called back, read in reverse

parts.note: a gibbet is a gallows

explanation.surface: A frivolous writer is accused of lying and recalled to the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storyteller?' means a teller of stories, a liar, not an author. IT reversed gives TI.
explanation.definitionFit: A flighty, gossipy person who never takes anything seriously is a scatterbrain.

clue.text: Evil remaining after good man departs

indicators.note: departs means the good man leaves the word

parts.note: still means remaining, as in still there
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good man

explanation.surface: Evil lingers once the good man has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm or wickedness, as in 'speak no ill', is a noun for evil.

clue.text: Not ringing with a ring?

definitions.meaning: a phone line that is busy gives no ringing tone
a couple betrothed to marry have an engagement ring

explanation.definitionFit: A busy telephone line and a betrothed person share this description.

clue.text: Ship carrying less ballast?

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed barge used to unload ships

explanation.surface: A question about a vessel's weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A barge for ferrying cargo shares its name with the comparative of not heavy.
